Mousavi and Karroubi remained under house arrest throughout.

title: Jaish al-Adl Attacks Kill 11 Police Officers in Rask; Iran-Pakistan Missile Exchange Follows
description: On December 15, 2023, Jaish al-Adl attacked a police station in Rask, Sistan-Baluchestan, killing 11 officers. On January 16, 2024, Iran launched ballistic missile and drone strikes on alleged Jaish al-Adl headquarters in Pakistan's Balochistan province, killing two children and wounding three others — a major breach of Pakistani sovereignty. Pakistan immediately expelled the Iranian ambassador and launched its own retaliatory strikes inside Iran two days later. The exchange represented the most serious Iran-Pakistan military confrontation in decades.

title: Houthi Red Sea Campaign: Iran Arms and Directs Attacks on Global Shipping
description: From November 2023, Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen launched hundreds of drone and missile attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea in solidarity with Gaza, causing a 90% reduction in container shipping through the Suez route by early 2024. US intelligence confirmed the IRGC Quds Force provided the drones, cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles used in the attacks and stationed trainers and operators in Yemen. The campaign disrupted an estimated 15% of global maritime trade and drew direct US and UK military strikes on Houthi targets.

title: Kerman ISIS Bombings Kill 95 at Soleimani Memorial — Deadliest Attack Since 1979
description: On January 3, 2024, the fourth anniversary of Qasem Soleimani's killing, two suicide bombers from Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISIS-K) detonated devices in a crowd of mourners at Soleimani's grave in Kerman, killing at least 95 people and wounding 284 — the deadliest terrorist attack inside Iran since the 1979 revolution. Iran had reportedly received advance warnings from the United States that it did not act upon. Iran blamed the attack on its regional enemies and used it to justify retaliatory strikes in Iraq, Syria, and Pakistan.

title: Iran Launches Direct Ballistic Missile Attack on Israel After Damascus Consulate Strike
description: On April 1, 2024, an Israeli airstrike on Iran's consulate in Damascus killed seven IRGC officers including two generals. On April 13–14, Iran retaliated with its first-ever direct military attack on Israeli territory, firing over 300 drones, ballistic missiles, and cruise missiles. The US, UK, France, Jordan, and Israel intercepted more than 99% of the projectiles. Israel conducted a limited retaliatory strike on Isfahan days later. The exchange established a direct military confrontation between Iran and Israel, marking a fundamental escalation in their decades-long shadow war.

title: Twelve-Day War: Israel Launches Massive Strikes on Iranian Nuclear Sites; 95 Killed
description: On June 13, 2025, Israel launched a major preemptive military campaign against Iran's nuclear infrastructure and IRGC leadership, deploying over 200 fighter jets in five waves of strikes targeting approximately 100 sites including Natanz, IRGC bases, and nuclear scientists' locations. Israel killed 30 Iranian generals and 9 nuclear scientists in the opening hours. Iran retaliated with over 500 ballistic missiles over 12 days. US forces joined with precision strikes on Fordow, Natanz, and Arak. A ceasefire brokered by Trump was announced June 24, 2025; hundreds of Iranian civilians were killed in Israeli strikes.

title: Sanctions-Induced Medical Humanitarian Crisis: Six Million Patients Denied Essential Medicines
description: By 2019, the reimposition of US maximum pressure sanctions had produced a severe medical humanitarian crisis inside Iran. Imports of medical supplies fell 60% between September 2018 and June 2019. Over six million patients with complex conditions — including hemophilia, multiple sclerosis, thalassemia, epilepsy, and cancer — faced acute drug shortages. Human Rights Watch documented the crisis in a major October 2019 report, concluding that US sanctions were 'seriously harming Iranians' right to health,' despite nominal humanitarian exemptions.

title: Ahmadinejad Wins Presidency; Guardian Council Engineers Hardliner Restoration
description: The Guardian Council's mass disqualification of reformist candidates in the 2004 parliamentary elections paved the way for Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's engineered presidential victory in June 2005. The hardline Basij and IRGC mobilized their institutional networks to deliver the vote, and independent analysts identified widespread irregularities. The Guardian Council's systematic exclusion of candidates from political competition — repeated in 2021 and 2024 — has been characterized by international human rights bodies as systematic political repression denying citizens free choice of government.

title: MEK Simultaneously Attacks Iranian Embassies in 13 Countries
description: In April 1992, the Mojahedin-e Khalq (MEK), operating from bases in Iraq, orchestrated simultaneous armed assaults on Iranian diplomatic missions in 13 countries, including the Iranian Mission to the United Nations in New York. The operation demonstrated the organization's logistical reach but killed no diplomats and generated more propaganda value than strategic impact. The attacks reinforced Iran's campaign to have the MEK internationally designated as a terrorist organization.

title: PJAK Resumes Armed Operations Against IRGC After Five-Year Lull
description: The Kurdish rebel group PJAK resumed armed operations against IRGC forces in Iranian Kurdistan in 2016 following a five-year period of relative quiescence since the 2011 ceasefire. Activities included ambushes of security personnel and an attempted close-quarter assassination of an Iranian member of parliament. The resumption coincided with renewed Turkish-PKK fighting and reflected PJAK's continued organizational capacity despite Iranian cross-border strikes on its bases in northern Iraq.

title: Guardian Council Disqualifies All Serious Candidates; Raisi Engineered to Presidency
description: For the June 2021 presidential election, the Guardian Council disqualified all significant reformist and moderate candidates, including former parliamentary speaker Ali Larijani and former first vice president Eshaq Jahangiri, ensuring hardline judiciary chief Ebrahim Raisi's victory. Voter turnout collapsed to a record-low 48.8%, reflecting mass public disillusionment. Human rights organizations noted that Raisi had been a member of the 'Death Commission' that ordered the 1988 prison massacres, yet faced no accountability.

title: Iran Ethnic Minorities — Kurds, Baluchis, Azeris — Bear Disproportionate Brunt of 2022 Crackdown
description: The UN Fact-Finding Mission on Iran's 2022 protests found that ethnic and religious minorities — particularly Kurds and Baluchis — were disproportionately killed, arrested, and subjected to summary executions during the Woman, Life, Freedom crackdown. The Mahsa Amini protests began in Kurdish areas; Zahedan's Bloody Friday massacre targeted Baluchi protesters. Human Rights Watch documented intensified repression of the Azeri minority by 2025, including arrests of cultural activists and forced closure of Azerbaijani-language publications.

title: Jaish al-Adl Kills 16 Soldiers; Iran-Pakistan Cross-Border Crisis
description: The killing of 16 Iranian soldiers by Jaish al-Adl in April 2024, compounded by the group's October 2024 twin attacks killing 6 IRGC and law enforcement personnel in Sistan-Baluchestan, exposed the persistent fragility of Iranian state control in its Baluchi southeast. These attacks followed Iran's January 2024 ballistic missile strike on Pakistani territory — itself retaliation for the December 2023 Rask police station attack. The escalation cycle demonstrated that the Baluchi insurgency constitutes a sustained, ongoing armed conflict rather than isolated incidents.

title: US-Israel Strikes Kill Khamenei; Iran Counter-Strikes Begin
description: On February 28, 2026, Israel and the United States launched a second major military campaign against Iran, assassinating Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and key political figure Ali Larijani. Iran launched counter-strikes against Israel, US military bases across the region, and Arab states hosting US forces. The attacks represented the most severe external military intervention in Iran since the Iran-Iraq War and triggered a multi-front conflict reshaping the regional order.

title: Fakhrizadeh Assassination: Mossad Kills Iran's Top Nuclear Weapons Scientist
description: Mohsen Fakhrizadeh, the father of Iran's military nuclear program and director of what Western intelligence agencies called the AMAD weapons project, was killed on November 27, 2020 near Tehran in an attack using a remote-controlled machine gun mounted on a Nissan pickup truck. Israel's Mossad was identified by Iranian and Israeli media as responsible. The killing followed four previous scientist assassinations attributed to Israel (2010–2012) and set back Iran's nuclear weapons-development expertise by depriving it of its most experienced technical leader.

title: ISIS-K Attack on Tehran Parliament and Khomeini Shrine Kills 17
description: On June 7, 2017, ISIS gunmen and suicide bombers carried out coordinated attacks on the Iranian parliament building and the mausoleum of Ayatollah Khomeini in southern Tehran, killing 17 people and wounding more than 40. It was the first major ISIS attack inside Iran and the first terrorist attack on the parliament since the MEK's 1981 bombing. ISIS's Amaq Agency released video of the attackers inside the parliament. Iran blamed Saudi Arabia for supporting ISIS and used the attack to justify its military operations in Iraq and Syria.

title: Iran Sanctions-Driven Economic Recession: Rial Loses 80%; Inflation Exceeds 40%
description: The cumulative effect of US and EU sanctions — including SWIFT exclusion in 2012 and oil export bans — produced a severe economic recession in Iran between 2012 and 2015. The rial lost over 80% of its value; inflation peaked above 40%; oil exports fell by more than half from 2.5 million to under 1 million barrels per day. GDP contracted significantly. The economic crisis drove popular pressure that enabled Rouhani's election and the eventual JCPOA negotiation, demonstrating how the sanctions directly shaped Iran's political and diplomatic choices.

title: Iran Crosses Nuclear Breakout Threshold: Enriches to 60%; Weeks From Weapons-Grade
description: By 2024, IAEA reports confirmed Iran was enriching uranium to 60% purity at Natanz and Fordow — one technical step below weapons-grade (90%) — and had accumulated enough fissile material that nuclear breakout time was estimated at under two weeks. Iran had exceeded every JCPOA limit since 2019. Advanced centrifuge cascades were operating at both declared and undisclosed sites. The nuclear impasse was a direct driver of the June 2025 Israeli military campaign that targeted Iran's enrichment infrastructure.

title: Iran Launches Lake Urmia Restoration Program to Save Dying Lake
description: In 2013, newly elected President Hassan Rouhani's government approved the Urmia Lake Restoration Program, an estimated $7 billion, ten-year effort to reverse the collapse of Lake Urmia, which had lost 96 percent of its volume in twenty years due to upstream water withdrawals. The program, coordinated by the Urmia Lake Restoration National Committee, targeted a 40 percent cut in regional agricultural water use and inter-basin water transfers to restore the lake to an ecological target level. Rouhani warned the lake's disappearance threatened up to 50 million Iranians with salt storms and displacement.
